title_en: A short ḥadīth: condition and reward
q_en: What must a person do, and what does he get for it?
not_yet: The chain of narrators in full and how it is judged: Lesson 73 shows the chain; its science is for another course.
Why each reward is “like” its deed: the text states it, you read it.
not_yet_ar: سِلْسِلَةُ الرُّوَاةِ كَامِلَةً وَالْحُكْمُ عَلَيْهَا: فِي الدَّرْسِ ٧٣ تَرَى الْإِسْنَادَ، وَعِلْمُهُ لِدَوْرَةٍ أُخْرَى.
لِمَاذَا يُشْبِهُ كُلُّ ثَوَابٍ عَمَلَهُ: النَّصُّ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ وَأَنْتَ تَقْرَأُ.

slides.head_en: Look: a deed and its reward
sents: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
Whoever comes to the lesson has a reward.
مَنْ دَلَّ أَخَاهُ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ ثَوَابٌ.
Whoever guides his brother to good has a reward.
Whoever helps his brother, Allah helps him.
لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحَدٌ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ.
No one speaks in the circle until he has listened.

lines: Sentences 1–3 begin with the same word. Which word? Does it point to one person?
الْجُمَلُ الثَّلَاثُ الْأُولَى تَبْدَأُ بِكَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ. مَا هِيَ؟ هَلْ تَدُلُّ عَلَى شَخْصٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
Find the deed (a verb) and the reward. Which little word opens the reward in sentences 1 and 2?
جِدِ الْعَمَلَ (فِعْلًا) وَجِدِ الثَّوَابَ. أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَفْتَحُ الثَّوَابَ فِي الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ الْأُولَيَيْنِ؟
Sentence 3: compare the two verbs. What do you see?
الْجُمْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَارِنْ بَيْنَ الْفِعْلَيْنِ. مَاذَا تَرَى؟
Sentence 4: which word says “no”, and which word says “until”?
الْجُمْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَنْفِي؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «إِلَى أَنْ»؟

slides.head_en: The frame of a short ḥadīth of conduct

cards.def_ar: مَنْ = كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ. وَالْفِعْلُ بَعْدَهَا هُوَ الْعَمَلُ.
cards.def_en: مَنْ = “whoever”. The verb after it is the deed.
The reward comes after the deed, and فَـ opens it.
The same verb returns; Allah is the doer.
After حَتَّى the verb ends in a short a.

slides.head_en: Four frames you will meet again and again
rows: لَا يَجْلِسُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ الْحَبِيبُ
slides.note: In the frame مَنْ + verb, the verb is in the past tense but the meaning is for any time: “whoever does …”.
slides.note_ar: الْفِعْلُ بَعْدَ «مَنْ» مَاضٍ فِي اللَّفْظِ، وَمَعْنَاهُ لِكُلِّ وَقْتٍ: «كُلُّ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ …».

slides.head_en: The reward is named with the deed’s own verb
slides.tip: Read the reward and you can tell the deed: it uses the same verb.
slides.tip_ar: إِذَا قَرَأْتَ الثَّوَابَ عَرَفْتَ الْعَمَلَ: الْفِعْلُ نَفْسُهُ.

slides.note: أَحَد + كُمْ: the ending ـكُمْ means “you” (many). أَحَدُكُمْ = one of you.
slides.note_ar: ـكُمْ ضَمِيرُ الْجَمْعِ لِلْمُخَاطَبِينَ. أَحَدُكُمْ = وَاحِدٌ مِنْكُمْ.

slides.head_en: What kind of text is this? How do you know?
slides.head_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
rows: a short ḥadīth: condition and reward
slides.note: The short ḥadīth of conduct has no commentary: only the saying, often with a few words of chain before it.
slides.note_ar: الْحَدِيثُ الْقَصِيرُ فِي الْأَدَبِ لَا شَرْحَ مَعَهُ: الْقَوْلُ فَقَطْ، وَقَدْ تَسْبِقُهُ كَلِمَاتٌ مِنَ الْإِسْنَادِ.

items: Whoever visits the Habib has a reward.
Whoever serves the guests has a reward.
Whoever teaches the people, Allah teaches him.
No one speaks until he has listened.
He has the like of his brother’s reward.
لَا يَجْلِسُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ الْحَبِيبُ
None of you sits until the Habib comes in.
Whoever honours a guest, Allah honours him.

slides.wrong: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ لَهُ أَجْرٌ
slides.why: The reward here is a whole sentence (لَهُ أَجْرٌ), so it must be opened with فَـ: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
slides.why_ar: الثَّوَابُ هُنَا جُمْلَةٌ، فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَفْتَحَهُ «فَ»: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.

lines: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ
"Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it."

slides.head_en: A ḥadīth: relieving a believer’s distress
lines: مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ الدُّنْيَا نَفَّسَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ
"Whoever relieves a believer of a distress of this world, Allah will relieve him of a distress of the Day of Resurrection,

slides.head_en: A ḥadīth: the reward answers the deed
lines: وَمَنْ يَسَّرَ عَلَى مُعْسِرٍ يَسَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فِى الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ
and whoever eases things for one in hardship, Allah will ease things for him in this world and the next,
وَمَنْ سَتَرَ مُسْلِمًا سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ فِى الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ
and whoever covers a Muslim's fault, Allah will cover his fault in this world and the next.

can: I can read a short ḥadīth of conduct and say the deed and the reward (مَنْ … فَلَهُ …).
I can see when the reward uses the same verb as the deed.
I can read لَا … أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى … and say what it means.
I can say what kind of text I am reading and how I know.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ حَدِيثًا قَصِيرًا فِي الْأَدَبِ وَأَقُولَ الْعَمَلَ وَالثَّوَابَ (مَنْ … فَلَهُ …).
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَرَى مَتَى يَكُونُ الثَّوَابُ مِنْ لَفْظِ الْعَمَلِ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «لَا … أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى …» وَأَقُولَ مَعْنَاهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقُولَ أَيَّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ أَقْرَأُ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتُ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Two sayings of the Prophet ﷺ in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Read them aloud, then answer.
lines: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ عَنِ النَّبِىِّ ﷺ قَالَ « لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ - أَوْ قَالَ لِجَارِهِ - مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ »
From Anas b. Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ: "None of you believes until he loves for his brother (or: his neighbour) what he loves for himself."
عَنْ أَبِى هُرَيْرَةَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ « مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ ...
From Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent."
sections.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Dār al-Jīl / Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut (Shamela 3.28 id 1786, vowelled, matches the print), 1/49: line 1 = ʿAbd al-Bāqī no. 45, line 2 = no. 47 (cut at a clause boundary: the quotation is left open, shown with "..."). The printed salutation formula is shown as the sign ﷺ; the source spelling (لاَ، لأَخِيهِ، النَّبِىِّ) is kept.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A short ḥadīth of conduct. Each saying opens with the Companion who reported it (عَنْ … عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ … قَالَ), then comes the saying itself, short and without commentary. The second one uses the frame مَنْ … فَـ.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.model: From Anas b. Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ: “None of you believes until he loves for his brother (or: his neighbour) what he loves for himself.”

items.en: Translate line 2.
items.model: From Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent ...”

items.en: Line 1: who is being addressed, and how do you know?
options: All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.
بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.
items.answer: All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.
items.model: All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.

items.en: True or false: line 1 says that one particular person does not believe.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ ١ إِنَّ شَخْصًا مُعَيَّنًا لَا يُؤْمِنُ.
items.model: False. أَحَد after لَا means “no one”: none of you believes until …
items.note: أَحَد after لَا means “no one”: none of you believes until …

items.en: Line 1: find the word that means “his neighbour”. What does the ـهِ mean?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «جَارَهُ». مَاذَا تَعْنِي ـهِ؟
options: بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.
All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.

items.en: Line 2: what two choices does the speaker have?
options: All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.
To speak good, or to keep silent.
بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.
items.answer: To speak good, or to keep silent.
items.model: To speak good, or to keep silent.

items.en: Read the ending of each word from its vowels and say why it has it.
items.ar_q: اِقْرَأْ نِهَايَةَ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ حَرَكَاتِهَا، وَقُلْ لِمَاذَا.
items.model: خَيْرًا: ـًا, what is said (it is the thing said, after فَلْيَقُلْ). الْيَوْمِ: ـِ, joined with وَ to اللَّهِ after بِـ. أَخِيهِ: ـِ, after the little word لِـ (the five nouns: أَخُو → أَخِي).

items.en: Which words in line 2 name the two things a believer holds to? Find the little word that joins them.
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ تُسَمِّيَانِ مَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُ؟ وَمَا الْحَرْفُ الَّذِي يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
options: بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.
All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.
items.answer: بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.
items.model: بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.

items.en: ★ The reporter says أَوْ قَالَ (“or he said”). What does this show about how the reporters worked?
items.ar_q: ★ يَقُولُ الرَّاوِي «أَوْ قَالَ». عَلَى مَاذَا يَدُلُّ ذَلِكَ فِي طَرِيقَةِ الرُّوَاةِ؟
items.model: He was not sure whether the Prophet ﷺ said “his brother” or “his neighbour”, so he gives both and tells us. This is honesty and care in passing on the words.

items.en: ★ Line 2 ends with “...”. Why does a copyist stop in the middle of a ḥadīth, and how does the reader know?
items.ar_q: ★ يَنْتَهِي السَّطْرُ ٢ بِنُقَطٍ. لِمَاذَا يَقِفُ النَّاسِخُ فِي وَسَطِ الْحَدِيثِ؟ وَكَيْفَ يَعْرِفُ الْقَارِئُ؟
items.model: The ḥadīth is longer: the copyist keeps only the part he needs. The open quotation mark and the dots tell the reader that more follows.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: after ʿIshāʾ in the ribāṭ. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
After ʿIshāʾ Ahmad sat with Umar in the ribāṭ.
وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ ضَيْفًا عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
And Umar said: Ahmad guided a guest to the way to the mosque.
فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ: هَلْ لِي أَجْرٌ؟
So Ahmad asked the Habib: Do I have a reward?
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: نَعَمْ يَا أَحْمَدُ، مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
The Habib said: Yes, Ahmad. Whoever guides to good has a reward.
And whoever helps his brother, Allah helps him.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ.
Then he said: None of you speaks in the majlis until he has listened.
فَسَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسَ الْحَبِيبِ وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ.
So Ahmad listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ أُمَّهُ عَلَى كِتَابٍ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، فَقَالَتْ: لَكَ ثَوَابٌ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
And in the morning Ahmad guided his mother to a book in the library, and she said: You have a reward, Ahmad.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom, and when?
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟ وَمَتَى؟
options: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.
items.answer: In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.
items.model: In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.

items.en: Who said that Ahmad guided someone? What had Ahmad done?
items.ar_q: مَنْ قَالَ إِنَّ أَحْمَدَ دَلَّ أَحَدًا؟ مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
items.model: Umar said it. Ahmad had guided a guest to the way to the mosque.

items.en: What did Ahmad ask in line 3?
options: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.

items.ar: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ
items.en: Line 4: which part is the deed and which part is the reward?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٤: أَيُّ جُزْءٍ هُوَ الْعَمَلُ؟ وَأَيُّ جُزْءٍ هُوَ الثَّوَابُ؟
items.model: The deed: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ (guided to good). The reward: فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.

items.en: Which little word opens the reward, and what does لَهُ mean?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَفْتَحُ الثَّوَابَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي «لَهُ»؟
options: In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.
He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
items.model: فَـ opens it. لَهُ = “he has” (for him).

items.en: Line 5: compare the two verbs. What is the same, and who is the doer of the second?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٥: قَارِنْ بَيْنَ الْفِعْلَيْنِ. مَا الْمُشْتَرَكُ؟ وَمَنْ فَاعِلُ الثَّانِي؟
items.model: The same verb. The doer of the second is Allah (اللَّهُ); the ending ـهُ is the man.

items.en: Translate line 6.
items.model: Then he said: None of you speaks in the majlis until he has listened.

items.en: True or false: the Habib tells them to speak first and listen later.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ: تَكَلَّمُوا أَوَّلًا ثُمَّ اسْمَعُوا.
items.model: False. حَتَّى means “until”: first listen, then speak.
items.note: حَتَّى means “until”: first listen, then speak.

items.en: What did Ahmad do in line 7?
options: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.
items.answer: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.
items.model: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.

items.en: What did his mother say in line 8, and why?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا قَالَتْ أُمُّهُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٨؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
items.model: “You have a reward, Ahmad”: because he guided her to a book in the library.

items.en: ★ Ahmad listened and did not speak. Which sentence of the Habib did he act on? Say it in your own words.

sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–135
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
